participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, running the meeting)
Derek Harris (setter, phones — second day on calls)
summary: Daily sales team meeting: a calendar mix-up where one prospect was double-booked across two closers' calendars in conflicting time zones, a wins round, projections, then two call reviews. Derek Harris reports his first day on the phones and is coached on disqualification criteria — the financial DQ, the four-figure qualifier, and routing unqualified leads to Primal University. Michael Brideau's call is reviewed: a prospect who was warm throughout, was asked for a $100 deposit when he said he needed to transfer funds from a precious-metals account, then went silent and hung up on the follow-up call. Andrew Musial's call is reviewed next: a 70-year-old prospect on Social Security of roughly $1,300 a month, supporting three daughters, who said he had budgeted about $500 and was placed on a 'Love It or Leave It' trial with a deposit. Chris coaches Andrew to open wallet before offering options and to schedule a decision call, and instructs him to tell the prospect that if he does not hear from him the card will be charged automatically for the six-payment plan. The meeting also covers two consumer-financing providers being onboarded, and ends in extended off-colour banter.
notable: AUTO-CHARGE ON SILENCE: Chris Klevan instructed Andrew on the trial follow-up — "just let them know that, like, if they don't, if you don't hear from them, that it's going to be a recurring payment, it's going to automatically charge their card for the six pay if they want it. We don't hear from them." The prospect in question is 70 and on a government pension.

TRIAL PRICING EXISTS: Andrew closed a prospect onto what he calls "Love It or Leave It" — "I got him on the Love It or Leave It" — a trial period of roughly a month and a half with a deposit and later top-up, against a prospect who said "I would have to be at something about half that amount... I would be more, do something about the $500 area."

VULNERABLE PROSPECT: the same prospect is 70, retired, "I'm on Social Security and I'm taking care of my family still. I have three daughters, and we have a large property here." Chris estimated the income himself: "it's probably like $1,300 a month. Something like that. Yeah, it's not a lot", and concluded after the fact "this is probably pretty tight for them, and we just don't know."

$100 DEPOSIT AS A BOOKING GATE: Michael Brideau on a live call — "Let's just do a super small deposit, even just $100 so we have something in, I can get you the documentation all done up, and that way we can have that call booked in for Trevor... Because technically I'm not supposed to book the onboarding call with Trevor until we have something in." The prospect stopped responding immediately after and hung up on the follow-up call the next day.

GUARANTEE AS STATED ON A LIVE CALL: "we're going to add eight kilograms to some of your main kettlebell lifts, okay, in the course of the six months... If we don't get you there in six months, Trevor will continue working with you for free until we do get you there." Chris reviewed this passage and did not correct it.

DRUG USE ON A SALES CALL: Michael Brideau recounted closing a prospect while under the influence of psilocybin — "Did I ever tell you I took what I thought was a microdose, and it wasn't, way more than a microdose? And I closed, I closed the guy" / "it wasn't like a crazy trip, but I was for sure tripping. I was like, oh, this is not sober Michael right now." Chris: "I remember this ridiculous call." The context suggests a previous employer (BIA/Birdvest), not Primal Instinct, but it was recounted approvingly on a Primal Instinct team call with two week-old hires present and Andrew asked to watch the recording.

CONSUMER FINANCING BEING ONBOARDED: Splitit is imminent — "anybody who has a credit card that has $6,000 available limit on it, put them through Splitit because then they'll be able to do it for 0% interest", expected "at the latest by Monday". A second financing provider was referred by Andrew and passed to the team. Klarna's 24-month option was also raised. This sits directly against Richard telling prospects on 6 and 9 July that there are no set payment plans.

SETTER DQ CRITERIA, STATED: Derek Harris — "if they seem financially qualified, like without the qualifier, I just send them through... one of the guys I DQ'd today was like a student. And so I just gave him the, hey, it's going to be like a four figure investment, premium coaching... Here's the Primal U stuff." Chris endorsed it: "that's like a big part of the job, being the gatekeeper of the calendar." Primal University is the standard destination for financially unqualified leads.
Richard Claessen requires a credit card to close: "they do have to have a credit card, because the guy that I had earlier today didn't even have a credit card."

Chris's diagnostic for money objections, stated cleanly: "always open wallet when it comes to finances, always... The last thing I want to do is sit there and overcome their fear for like an hour to find out they can't even make it work financially", and the should-versus-how distinction as the branch point between uncertainty and affordability.

Michael Brideau is taking prospect calls until midnight from Brazil on a Colombian sleep schedule and reports every slot the previous day no-showed; he has started phoning every booked prospect to confirm.
Adam A. reports the lead source is a Facebook audience of several hundred thousand that nobody has been messaging, alongside the existing channel.
Adam A. is part-way through a personal training certification and has chosen strength and conditioning as his niche — relevant because he is also the setter who speaks as Trevor in voice messages.
Coaching artefact worth noting: Chris advises minimising head movement on camera, citing an Instagram post claiming closers who move their heads least collect more.
